differences.what: Massing (T-2485): a low log building, gable end to the eye, with the back slope and a short side receding to the right. Drawn gable 1419-1495 px wide with the side to about 1512, eave 731, apex 712, grade about 755; the render's gable 1418-1497 and side to about 1513, eave about 730, apex about 711, grade about 755. Built at 6.2 m across the gable, 1.95 m to the eave and 27 degrees, read off the plate's proportions.

Openings: two small openings side by side under the east gable's eave, a square one toward the front and a round-headed one toward the back (x 1440-1446 and 1469-1475, y 733-741 px). Built as two of the archetype's small square lights at the same places; the round head of the back one is not built, at 6 px it is a single dark spot in the render's pixels too.
Walls: horizontal log courses with the ends out at the corners, as built.
Roof: plain gable, no stack, as built.
Tone: the engraving is monochrome, so the log and roof colours are not read from it.
The two horses before it and the picket paling behind them at the left: not this record. Animals are not built, and the paling is drawn where the house's green (kinzie_house_1812_green) runs.
The west gable and the south front, with the door: the plate does not see them.
